cards.text: Isaiah son of Amoz, who saw the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 1:1), is telling this one himself. It's the year King Uzziah of Judah died (2 Chronicles 26:1). And Isaiah says he saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted.

cards.question: Isaiah sees the Lord on a high, exalted throne. What fills the temple?

cards.text: Above the Lord stand seraphim, each one with SIX WINGS. Friend, I've got one mustache, and I thought I was the most equipped guy in the room.

cards.question: Each seraph above the throne uses all six of its wings for flying.

cards.text: Two wings cover their faces, two cover their feet, and two do the flying. And the seraphim are calling out to one another about the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The seraphim above the throne are calling out to one another. They call out that the LORD of Hosts is ___.

cards.text: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory." Friend, if I heard that in my bakery, my mustache would freeze mid-stamp.

cards.question: At the sound of the seraphim's voices, the temple's doorposts and thresholds shake.

cards.text: And on top of that, the temple is filled with smoke.

Then Isaiah says, "Woe is me, for I am ruined…" because his eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts. I get it, friend: an important guest walks into my bakery and suddenly I see EVERY crumb on my apron.

cards.question: Standing before the King, what does Isaiah say about himself?

answers.text: He is a man of unclean lips
He is a man of slow speech
He is the least in his father's house

cards.question: Isaiah says he is the only one with unclean lips, and his people are just fine.

cards.text: Then one of the seraphim flies to Isaiah, holding a glowing coal from the altar. He took it with tongs, and friend, I respect ANYBODY who reaches for the tongs.

cards.question: With the glowing coal from the altar, the seraph touches Isaiah's ___.
After the coal touches Isaiah, what does the seraph tell him?

cards.text: The seraph says more: one touch of that coal, and the man who just said "I am ruined" hears that his sin is atoned for.
Then Isaiah hears the voice of the Lord: "Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?" That's the kind of question where a whole room suddenly gets REAL interested in the floor.

cards.question: The Lord asks whom He should send. How does Isaiah answer?

answers.text: He asks Him to send someone else

cards.text: Isaiah has said he'll go, and now the Lord gives him the message, and I'll be honest, friend, this one's heavy. He tells Isaiah to go and tell this people to be ever hearing and ever seeing.

cards.question: In the Lord's message, this people keeps hearing and keeps seeing. What do they never do?

cards.text: Then the Lord says, "Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes." Hearts, ears AND eyes.

cards.question: The Lord says that otherwise the people might see, hear and understand with their hearts. Then what might they do?

cards.text: Isaiah asks, "How long, O Lord?" Friend, back in the junk drawer I spent years stuck in, I asked the dust that same question every single day.

cards.question: When Isaiah asks how long, the Lord says only until the next king takes the throne.
Isaiah asks the Lord how long. The Lord answers until the cities lie ruined, and until the houses are left ___.

cards.text: And the Lord's not done answering: "until the LORD has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken."

cards.question: The Lord says that though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again.

cards.text: Then the Lord gives a picture you can SEE: terebinth and oak trees, felled. Buttercup, one of my cookie cutter kids, always explained everything with something you could see.

cards.question: The Lord says the holy seed will be in the land like what felled terebinths and oaks leave behind. What is it?
